cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put your gnome back by the pond. I've brought him home in a box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does he need a box?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: His head and body are packed separately. I'll glue them before you have to look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's Dad's gnome. Don't replace any part of him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll use the broken pieces, then. One ear's missing; help me look in the box before I start.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 manages homecoming, A3 buffers breakage by promising unseen repair, and A5 yields to B inherited-object concern by inviting B into the search before repair.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 box question causes A3 separated pieces; B4 no replacement condition causes A5 original pieces and missing-ear disclosure.

relationship.evidence: B4 names Dad as the source of attachment and prioritises original material over a seamless substitute.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns A3 hidden repair into shared inspection while revealing that even the return of pieces is incomplete.

specificity.evidence: A1 gnome and pond, A3 separate head/body and B4 inherited attachment establish the sentimental repair.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 each clause does necessary work: preserve originals, reveal a missing part, and ask for help before altering anything.
